newsitem.title: USA: Controversy over singer clouds Miami festival.
newsitem.headline: Controversy over singer clouds Miami festival.

text.p: Controversy clouded Miami's giant Calle Ocho street fair on Friday after organisers of this weekend's event banned a Puerto Rican singer for actions considered to be too friendly toward Cuba's government.

Puerto Rican singer Andy Montanez was banned from Calle Ocho (Eighth Street), the nation's largest Latin American festival, for hugging Silvio Rodriguez, a Cuban folk singer considered to be a supporter of Cuban President Fidel Castro, during a news conference in Puerto Rico on Monday.

Montanez could not be reached for comment and the Kiwanis Club of Little Havana, which sponsors the fair, declined to discuss the action. But some area Puerto Rican leaders said they were outraged and the Puerto Rican Chamber of South Florida, a business group, said it might stage a protest on Sunday.

The flap over Montanez was only the latest political controversy stemming from the festival, an annual weekend of food, games and music that draws about a million people to Miami's Little Havana neighbourhood.

The 23-block stretch of Eighth Street that hosts the party is the spiritual heart of the Cuban-American community, which is staunchly opposed to Castro's government, and its exile sponsors have shown no hesitation in mixing politics with the event.
Montanez has appeared at Calle Ocho several times but he has also been barred from the event before. He was one of three musical acts banned in 1989.

Last year a jury awarded Brazilian singer Denise de Kalafe, also banned that year, a $2.68 million settlement in a suit she filed claiming Calle Ocho organisers had done grave harm to her career by banning her.
A year ago Calle Ocho was cancelled as the Cuban-American community mourned four exiles belonging to the Brothers to the Rescue group shot down a few weeks earlier by Cuban jets.
